author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose storage-induced loading stutter in PS2 games
summary: Correlate pauses with disc reads, area transitions, cache misses, and Android storage location by replaying one loading boundary from internal and removable storage while preserving image identity and emulator settings.
heroAlt: PCSX2 Open Data Directory command used to inspect the storage paths involved in a stutter test

blocks.text: Tie each pause to a reproducible read boundary

Storage-related stutter usually follows a consistent area transition, texture stream, FMV start, or first access to a file. It differs from regular frame-pacing spikes and from thermal decline that follows elapsed time. Choose a normal save before one repeatable loading boundary, record the image hash, and compare the same verified file on internal storage with a documented removable-storage copy.
Copy rather than move the only disc image, and never benchmark a card that is disconnecting or reporting filesystem errors. Preserve saves and profiles before changing storage paths.
Prepare identical images on two storage paths

items: A verified PS2 image with a recorded cryptographic hash.
A normal save before a deterministic loading transition.
Enough internal space for a temporary test copy.
A healthy removable device and stable Android folder permission if used.
One unchanged renderer, profile, cache state, and timing method.

blocks.text: Compare repeated boundaries and storage locations

items: 1. Run the boundary twice from its current location and mark each pause timestamp.
2. Record Android storage path, free space, connection type, and any read-error log entries.
3. Copy the image to internal storage without modifying the original.
4. Verify the copied file hash matches the source exactly.
5. Refresh the library, select the internal copy, and replay the same boundary twice.
6. Compare pause duration and recurrence while keeping cache state equivalent.
7. Test a second loading boundary to avoid a one-scene conclusion.
8. Remove the temporary duplicate only after the preferred path and save behavior are confirmed.

blocks.text: A repeatable pause that shrinks materially with the identical file on internal storage supports an I/O or access-path issue. If both locations behave alike, the boundary may be dominated by emulated decompression, shader creation, or game logic. Hash equality prevents a damaged or different revision from contaminating the comparison.
The result is valid when file identity, route, cache, and emulator configuration match across both locations.

items: Source and copied disc images have identical hashes.
The same save and loading boundary are replayed.
No renderer, resolution, or speed setting changes.
At least two passes per location show the same pattern.
Logs contain no unresolved read or permission errors.
Android permission expires between passes: reauthorize and restart the comparison.
The first run warms shaders while the second tests storage: normalize cache state.
The removable device reconnects or changes mount path: stop and repair access.
Temperature differs substantially: cool and rerun.

blocks.text: Point the library back to the chosen stable image, verify one normal launch and save load, then remove only the confirmed temporary duplicate. Restore ordinary media permissions and retain the hash and path record for future storage migrations.
Area transitions can combine several costs

One doorway may trigger disc reads, decompression, shader compilation, and a large burst of emulated work. Storage sensitivity is established by the controlled location response, not by the fact that a loading icon appeared.
